verdict.rationale: Oneleet documents per-provider integration pages for AWS (via AssumeRole, with tag-based exclusion and revocation by deleting the role), GitHub (configuration, user access and Dependabot, without repository-content access) and Google Workspace (user accounts and Gmail settings). That covers the cloud, code-hosting and identity parts of the story. MDM is Oneleet's own MDM product rather than a connector to an existing one, and Fieldwork's connector claim is vague marketing. missing for 10: HR integrations, ticketing integrations, connectors to third-party MDMs, an evidenced browsable catalog breadth, explicit documentation of read-only scopes per integration, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an IT admin, I can connect my real stack — cloud providers, identity, HR, code hosting, MDM, ticketing — through a documented integrations catalog with read-only scopes

citations.quote: Oneleet uses the AWS AssumeRole API to work with AWS resources
You can use it to monitor your GitHub configuration, user access, and Dependabot vulnerabilities. It does not require access to repository contents.
Oneleet currently monitors the following on Google Workspace: User accounts, GMail settings
You can prevent AWS resources from being read into Oneleet by adding the tag `oneleet-ignore=true` for resources which support tagging.
